name: How long does it take to build an in-law suite in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to build an in-law suite in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How long does it take to build an in-law suite in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A realistic in-law suite timeline includes design, permitting, and construction, not just the build phase. A conversion can move faster because it uses an existing structure, while a detached suite usually takes longer due to grading, foundation, framing, and utility work. In the Los Angeles area, city review and plan corrections can add significant time before construction even begins. Older homes may also slow the schedule if electrical, plumbing, or structural upgrades are needed. Homeowners should ask for a timeline that breaks down each phase: feasibility, design, permit review, procurement, and field construction. That makes delays easier to spot early. If the site is complex or the city asks for revisions, the schedule should include extra buffer time from the start.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most in-law suite projects take longer than homeowners expect because design, permitting, and inspections can take months before construction starts. A conversion is usually faster than a detached new build. The total timeline depends on city review speed, utility work, and whether the project needs structural changes or site prep.
